intent.raw_query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX

experiences.name: Gyeongbokgung Palace & Hanbok Experience
experiences.description: Explore the iconic Joseon-era palace and rent a traditional Hanbok for free entry and stunning photos. Arrive early to catch the ceremonial guard changing. Located centrally, making it easy to access from most hotels in the Jongno or Insadong area. Since the flight arrives late on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 morning as a strong cultural opener.

experiences.name: Gwangjang Market Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into one of Seoul's oldest and most vibrant traditional markets. Sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap, tteokbokki, and fresh yukhoe (beef tartare). Best experienced at lunch when stalls are fully active. Stay near Jongno or Euljiro to walk here easily and maximize time on Day 2 afternoon after the palace visit.

experiences.name: Hongdae K-Culture Nightlife & Street Performance Walk
experiences.description: Experience the beating heart of Korean youth culture, K-pop, and indie music in Hongdae. Enjoy free street performances, visit K-pop merchandise shops, explore themed cafes, and dine at trendy local eateries. Consider staying in Mapo-gu or Sinchon to be within walking distance. Best done mid-trip when you're settled in. Budget includes dinner and a couple of drinks.

experiences.name: Insadong Teahouse & Craft Culture Stroll
experiences.description: Wander through Insadong's charming alleyways filled with traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Stop at Ssamziegil for indie designer goods and enjoy a bowl of patbingsu or traditional Korean tea. This area is walkable from Gyeongbokgung, making it ideal to combine on the same day. A relaxed, immersive cultural afternoon experience.

experiences.name: Myeongdong Street Food & K-Beauty Shopping
experiences.description: Spend an evening in Myeongdong sampling street food skewers, egg bread, lobster tails, and Korean corn dogs while browsing K-beauty flagship stores like Innisfree, Etude House, and Olive Young. This is a must for K-culture enthusiasts. Easily accessible by subway from most central hotels. Plan this for mid-to-late trip when you know your skincare and snack preferences.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Seoul, South Korea
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Incheon International Airport at 13:00. Take the AREX express train (₩9,500) to Seoul Station, then subway to Jongno-gu. Check in to Jongno-gu Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a gentle orientation walk around Insadong-gil street — browse traditional craft shops, tea houses, and street stalls to get your bearings in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Gwanghwamun Square to see the illuminated statue of King Sejong and the Gyeongbokgung Palace gates lit up at dusk. Explore the nearby Cheonggyecheon Stream walkway — beautifully lit in winter — for a relaxing first evening in Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Incheon Airport convenience store (CU/GS25)
meals.lunch: Quick meal at Seoul Station food court or a convenience store kimbap and ramyeon (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.dinner: Gwanghwamun Jip or a local pojangmacha (street tent bar) near Insadong for tteokbokki, sundae, and odeng (₩6,000–9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-money card at the airport or any convenience store (₩2,500 deposit). Load ₩30,000–50,000 to start. December in Seoul is cold (around -2°C to 5°C), so wear thermal layers. Keep receipts for VAT refund eligibility on purchases over ₩30,000.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace (₩3,000 entry) when it opens at 09:00. Witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 10:00 and 14:00 (free to watch). Explore the vast palace grounds and the beautiful Hyangwonjeong Pavilion, especially scenic dusted with winter frost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Folk Museum of Korea inside the palace grounds (free entry). Then head to Bukchon Hanok Village — a 15-minute walk — to wander the traditional hanok alleyways and enjoy panoramic city views. Consider renting a hanbok (₩10,000–15,000/hour) for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Insadong for dinner and evening browsing. Explore Ssamziegil — a quirky indie shopping courtyard with local art, handmade goods, and snacks. Browse the many small galleries and pick up affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby bakery like Paris Baguette/Tous Les Jours (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Gimbap Cheonguk or a local kimbap nara near Gyeongbokgung for a filling set meal (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.dinner: Insadong Teahouse alley — try traditional bingsu or hotteok, then a bowl of doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) at a local restaurant (₩7,000–9,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. Since today is Wednesday it is open. Wear comfortable shoes for extensive walking on cobblestones. The palace grounds cover 410,000 sqm so plan 2–3 hours minimum.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Changdeokgung Palace (₩3,000 entry), a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Book a guided Secret Garden (Huwon) tour in advance online (₩5,000 additional) — the winter garden with bare trees and frozen ponds is hauntingly beautiful. Tours run at specific times so check the schedule.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Changgyeonggung Palace next door (₩1,000 entry) — often overlooked by tourists and very peaceful. Then explore Naksan Park nearby for free city views and a walk along the old Seoul City Wall ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — free to enter the exterior and plaza. The futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building is dramatically lit at night. Browse the surrounding Dongdaemun shopping district and night markets that come alive after dark.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — triangle kimbap, boiled egg, and canned coffee (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Ikseon-dong Hanok Village nearby — trendy but affordable lunch spots, try a small Korean brunch cafe for bibimbap or dosirak (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun night market street food — tteokbokki, hotteok, gyeranppang (egg bread), and fish cake skewers (₩5,000–8,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Changdeokgung Secret Garden tours have limited spots — book via the official website at least a day ahead. Ikseon-dong is a charming mix of old hanok alleys and hip cafes, worth a short detour between palaces.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Gwangjang Market — one of Seoul's oldest and most authentic traditional markets. This is a must for food lovers. Try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (tiny addictive rice rolls), and yukhoe (beef tartare) directly from the market stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Cheonggyecheon Stream from its source near Gwanghwamun all the way east — a peaceful 6km urban stream walk. Visit the Cheonggyecheon Museum (free) to learn about the stream's remarkable restoration. Then explore the Euljiro district, Seoul's creative hub full of old printing shops, neon-lit cafes, and indie bars.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Myeongdong for the famous street food evening scene. Try Korean street snacks — tornado potato, lobster grilled cheese, hotteok, and Korean fried chicken. Browse the cosmetics shops for budget K-beauty finds (many have free samples).

meals.breakfast: Gwangjang Market — mayak gimbap and a bowl of kongnamul gukbap (bean sprout rice soup) (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.lunch: Street food along Cheonggyecheon or a local bunsik (Korean snack restaurant) for ramyeon and tteokbokki combo (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food feast — budget ₩8,000–12,000 for a satisfying variety of skewers, pancakes, and snacks

day_by_day.notes: Gwangjang Market is most vibrant in the morning. Bring cash as many stalls are cash-only. Myeongdong gets very crowded on Friday evenings — embrace the energy! Many cosmetic brands like Innisfree, Etude House, and The Face Shop offer significant discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park (free entry, accessible by subway to Gupabal or Dobongsan station). Hike one of the beginner-friendly trails such as the Bukhansanseong Fortress trail. The winter scenery with snow-dusted granite peaks is spectacular. Wear proper winter hiking shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall (₩3,000) — a sobering but important museum documenting Korea's independence movement and Japanese colonial period. Very educational for understanding modern Korean identity and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hongdae neighbourhood — Seoul's youth culture and indie music hub. Walk the main streets, catch a free busking performance (common even in winter weekends), browse vintage clothing shops, and soak in the vibrant K-culture atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pack convenience store kimbap and thermos of hot tea for the hike (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Mountain hiker's staple — cup ramyeon at a trail rest stop shelter (₩1,500) or pack your own snacks
meals.dinner: Hongdae — try a local Korean BBQ restaurant for samgyeopsal (pork belly) — look for all-you-can-eat options around ₩12,000–15,000 per person, very popular in this area

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike early (by 09:00) as winter days are short with sunset around 17:20. Bring hand warmers and dress in layers. Bukhansan is one of the world's most visited national parks per unit area — weekends can be busy but trails are well-marked.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located right in Jongno-gu near your hotel (free entry). In December it is beautifully decorated with lanterns for the winter season. Attend a morning ceremony if you wake early enough (around 04:00 or 10:00). Explore the temple grounds peacefully.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Gyeonghuigung Palace (free entry) — the least visited of Seoul's five grand palaces, offering a quiet and authentic experience. Then head to Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a charming neighbourhood of independent cafes, bookshops, and art studios in restored hanok buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Namsan Seoul Tower (N Seoul Tower) via the free Namsan Cable Car shuttle bus from Chungmuro station. Cable car costs ₩9,500 return. The tower observation deck costs ₩16,000 but the surrounding fortress wall walk and city views from the hill base are free and stunning at night.

meals.breakfast: Seochon Village independent cafe — artisan coffee and Korean-style toast with egg (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Gyeonghuigung area local restaurant — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) set with rice and banchan side dishes (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon or Myeongdong area — affordable Korean fried chicken (chimaek) with beer at a local chicken restaurant (₩15,000–18,000 for two sharing)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple's lantern decorations are particularly beautiful in the evening — consider revisiting after dark. Namsan Tower is a classic Seoul experience; the love lock fence area is free to visit. Dress very warmly as the hilltop is significantly colder and windier than the city below.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Noryangjin Fish Market — one of Seoul's largest wholesale fish markets. Arrive early (by 08:00) to see the auction atmosphere. You can buy fresh seafood directly from vendors and have it prepared at upstairs restaurants for a small cooking fee. Very affordable and authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Han River to Yeouido — Seoul's financial and political island. Walk along the Yeouido Hangang Park riverside (free). Visit the National Assembly building exterior and the 63 Building area. Take in views of the frozen or flowing Han River depending on winter temperatures.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gangnam district via subway — explore the famous Gangnam-daero boulevard immortalized in PSY's song. Visit COEX Mall (free to enter) — an enormous underground shopping complex. Check out the stunning COEX Library (Starfield Library) — a free public space with floor-to-ceiling bookshelves, a true Seoul landmark.

meals.breakfast: Noryangjin Fish Market — fresh sashimi breakfast set with miso soup and rice (₩10,000–15,000, extremely fresh and worth it)
meals.lunch: Yeouido — convenience store or local bunsik restaurant near the park (₩4,000–6,000)
meals.dinner: Gangnam area — explore the back alleys behind Gangnam station for affordable local restaurants; try galbi tang (short rib soup) or kimchi jjigae (₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: Noryangjin Fish Market operates 24 hours but is most lively early morning. Bring cash for the market. The COEX Starfield Library is free but photography rules apply — be respectful. Gangnam is pricier than Jongno-gu so stick to side streets for budget eating.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan (free entry) — one of Asia's largest museums with incredible artifacts from Korean history spanning 5,000 years. Plan at least 3 hours here. Highlights include the Gilt-bronze Maitreya Bodhisattva and the Celadon collections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the War Memorial of Korea nearby (free entry to the main building and outdoor exhibits). The outdoor display of military equipment, aircraft, and warships is impressive and sobering. The indoor exhibits cover Korean War history with emotional depth.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Itaewon neighbourhood — Seoul's most international district. Browse the eclectic mix of vintage shops, international restaurants, and antique dealers on Antique Furniture Street. Visit Haebangchon (HBC) — a hillside neighbourhood with a village atmosphere and great affordable eateries.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or nearby convenience store (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: National Museum of Korea cafeteria — affordable Korean set meals in a beautiful setting (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Haebangchon (HBC) — try a local Korean restaurant or the affordable international options; Korean army stew (budae jjigae) is perfect for cold winter evenings (₩8,000–10,000)

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Korea is closed on Mondays — today is Tuesday so it is open. Both museums are free and represent extraordinary value. Itaewon has become more locally-oriented in recent years with great independent businesses replacing chain stores.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Lotte World Tower area in Jamsil — walk around the base of Korea's tallest skyscraper (free). Visit Seokchon Lake nearby — a beautiful urban lake that is especially magical in winter. Explore Lotte World Folk Museum (₩5,000) inside Lotte World for a fun look at Korean traditional culture through dioramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Olympic Park (free entry to the park grounds) — built for the 1988 Seoul Olympics. Walk the sculpture garden featuring 200+ outdoor artworks, visit the historic Mongchon Toseong earthen fortress wall, and enjoy the peaceful winter park atmosphere away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jongno-gu and explore the Pimatgol alley — a historic narrow alleyway running parallel to Jongno avenue, historically used by commoners to avoid bowing to passing nobles on horseback. Now lined with traditional restaurants and pojangmacha tents.

meals.breakfast: Jamsil area bakery or convenience store (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Olympic Park area — packed lunch from a nearby convenience store or a local restaurant near the park entrance (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Pimatgol alley — traditional Korean food in a historic setting; try haemul pajeon (seafood scallion pancake) and makgeolli (rice wine) for an authentic experience (₩10,000–14,000)

day_by_day.notes: Lotte World amusement park itself is expensive (₩62,000+) — skip it and enjoy the free surrounding areas. Olympic Park is large (1.4km²) so wear comfortable shoes. Pimatgol is one of Seoul's most atmospheric dining streets — go hungry!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Deoksugung Palace (₩1,000 entry) — the smallest of Seoul's five palaces but uniquely blends traditional Korean and Western architecture. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at the Daehanmun Gate (10:00, 14:00, 15:30 — free). The palace is particularly atmospheric in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Seoul Museum of History (free entry) near Gyeonghuigung. Then explore Gwanghwamun Square — Seoul's main plaza will likely have Christmas decorations and events. Visit the nearby Sejong Center for the Performing Arts to check for affordable or free performances.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul is celebrated enthusiastically — Koreans treat it as a romantic and festive occasion. Head to Myeongdong Cathedral (free) for the Christmas Eve atmosphere and possible mass service. Then enjoy the festively decorated Myeongdong streets and street food scene which will be buzzing with energy.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Korean breakfast at a local restaurant — kongnamul haejangguk (hangover soup, popular for breakfast) (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.lunch: Deoksugung area — local dosirak (Korean lunch box) restaurant or a nearby bunsik spot (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve treat — splurge slightly at a Korean BBQ restaurant in Myeongdong for galbi (beef short ribs) — budget ₩20,000–25,000 for a festive celebration meal

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is very popular in Seoul — Myeongdong will be extremely crowded but wonderfully festive. Myeongdong Cathedral is a beautiful Gothic landmark worth visiting regardless of faith. Many shops and restaurants will have special Christmas promotions. Book dinner early or be prepared to queue.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea. Visit Jogyesa Temple again for the peaceful morning atmosphere — a beautiful contrast to the commercial Christmas celebrations. Then walk through the quiet morning streets of Jongno-gu and Insadong, which take on a calm, reflective quality on the holiday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the subway to Mangwon Market in Mapo-gu — a beloved local market less touristy than Gwangjang, popular with Seoul residents. Browse seasonal produce, street food, and local goods. Then walk along the Mangwon Hangang Park riverside for fresh air and Han River views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Sinchon and Yonsei University area — a vibrant university district with affordable eateries, indie bookshops, and a lively student atmosphere even on holidays. Walk through the beautiful Yonsei University campus, one of Korea's most picturesque.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — many places may have reduced hours on Christmas morning (₩3,000–4,000)
meals.lunch: Mangwon Market — fresh street food including tteokbokki, sundae, and freshly made mandu (dumplings) (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Sinchon area university district — affordable Korean comfort food; try a local sundubu jjigae restaurant or a student-friendly Korean BBQ spot (₩8,000–12,000)

day_by_day.notes: Some attractions may have modified hours on Christmas Day — check ahead. Many Korean-owned restaurants remain open as Christmas is not a traditional Korean holiday (though widely celebrated). The Mangwon area is beloved by Seoul locals and offers an authentic non-touristy experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Palace Museum of Korea (free entry) — located within the Gyeongbokgung grounds, separate from the palace itself. Excellent collection of royal artifacts, furniture, and ceremonial objects. Then visit the National Hangeul Museum (free, nearby) dedicated to the Korean alphabet — fascinating for K-culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Euljiro 3-ga area — Seoul's most interesting urban renewal district where old metalworking shops sit alongside trendy cafes and art spaces. Visit the Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) main branch for free or low-cost exhibitions. Walk through the Mugyo-dong area near City Hall.
day_by_day.evening: Final proper evening in Seoul — return to your favourite neighbourhood for a farewell dinner. Consider revisiting Insadong or Gwangjang Market. End the evening with a walk along the illuminated Cheonggyecheon Stream, reflecting on your 13 days in Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Insadong traditional tea house — traditional Korean tea and tteok (rice cakes) for a cultural breakfast experience (₩6,000–8,000)
meals.lunch: Euljiro area — try one of the famous old-school restaurants that have survived decades; look for places with handwritten menus and long queues of locals (₩7,000–9,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a proper sit-down Korean meal; try samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) at a traditional restaurant in Jongno-gu (₩14,000–16,000) — warming and nourishing for the cold weather

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any remaining souvenir shopping. Good budget souvenir spots: Insadong (traditional crafts), Gwangjang Market (fabric and traditional goods), Myeongdong (K-beauty). Keep receipts for VAT refunds at the airport (minimum purchase ₩30,000 per store). Pack carefully tonight as you depart tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul. Take a last peaceful walk around your Jongno-gu neighbourhood — perhaps one final visit to Jogyesa Temple or a quiet coffee at a local cafe. Check out of the Jongno-gu Boutique Stay (standard checkout is 11:00 — confirm with the hotel). Store luggage at the hotel if needed for a few extra hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with ample time. Take the subway to Seoul Station and board the AREX express train to Incheon Airport (₩9,500, approximately 43 minutes). Arrive at least 3 hours before international departure. Complete VAT refund claims at the airport tax refund counters before check-in or at customs after check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Browse duty-free shops at Incheon Airport — one of the world's best airports with excellent food options, a traditional Korean cultural zone, and free luggage storage and shower facilities. Board your flight home with incredible memories of Seoul.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — go to a local gukbap (rice soup) restaurant near the hotel for a hearty send-off meal; try seolleongtang (ox bone broth soup) (₩9,000–11,000)
meals.lunch: Seoul Station food court or convenience store before boarding the AREX train (₩4,000–7,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — treat yourself to a sit-down meal at one of the airport restaurants; Korean options are reasonably priced for an international airport (₩10,000–15,000)

day_by_day.notes: Return your T-money card at the airport or keep it for future trips (the deposit is refundable minus a small fee). Incheon Airport has a free cultural experience zone with traditional Korean performances and hands-on activities if you have time before your flight. Double-check your flight terminal (Terminal 1 or Terminal 2) as Incheon has two separate terminals connected by a shuttle train.

trip_options.title: Classic Seoul, South Korea Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from Incheon Airport to Jongno-gu hotel via AREX express train (~43 min) then subway or taxi. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around Insadong Street, just minutes from Jongno-gu. Browse traditional tea houses, Korean craft shops, and galleries. Visit Ssamziegil, a quirky open-air complex with indie boutiques and street food stalls — perfect for easing into Seoul.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Cheonggyecheon Stream for a peaceful illuminated walk along the canal, especially beautiful in December with winter light festivals. End the evening at nearby Gwangjang Market for an authentic first taste of Korean street food culture.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab kimbap or tteokbokki from a street stall near Insadong (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Gwangjang Market — try bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak kimbap, and yukhoe (raw beef) from market vendors (₩15,000–25,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag will be a factor. Exchange currency at the airport or use a Wise/local ATM. Pick up a T-money card at the airport convenience store for seamless transit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Gyeongbokgung Palace when it opens at 9:00 AM. Explore the grand main halls, the National Folk Museum of Korea within the palace grounds, and witness the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony (10:00 AM & 2:00 PM). Rent a hanbok at a nearby shop for free palace entry and great photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk north to Bukchon Hanok Village — a beautifully preserved neighborhood of traditional Korean hanok houses. Wander the narrow alleys, enjoy the contrast of ancient architecture against the city skyline, and pop into small galleries and craft workshops along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Samcheong-dong for dinner and evening exploration. This charming neighborhood has art galleries, cozy cafes, and boutique restaurants. Browse the lit-up streets after dinner for a romantic winter atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — try a Korean-style egg toast (gyeran toast) from a street cart (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang near Gyeongbokgung — famous ginseng chicken soup, warming and perfect for winter (₩17,000)
meals.dinner: Samcheong-dong restaurant — try doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) set meal at a traditional Korean restaurant (₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays — Wednesday is perfect. Dress warmly; December temperatures in Seoul average -2°C to 5°C. Hanbok rental shops are clustered near the palace's south gate.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Changdeokgung Palace and its famous Secret Garden (Huwon). This UNESCO World Heritage Site requires a guided tour for the garden — book in advance. The natural landscape and traditional pavilions are stunning even in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Changgyeonggung Palace next door (combined ticket available), then walk to Ikseon-dong Hanok Village — a trendier, younger take on hanok culture with indie cafes, vintage shops, and fusion restaurants tucked into traditional alleyways.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at Naksan Park for panoramic night views of Seoul from atop the old city wall. Walk a section of the Seoul City Wall trail illuminated at night. Return via Hyehwa Station area (Daehangno) for theater district vibes and street performances.

meals.breakfast: Ikseon-dong café — artisan coffee and Korean-style croissant or red bean pastry (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Jongno-gu area — sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) at a local pojangmacha or restaurant (₩9,000–13,000)
meals.dinner: Daehangno area — galbi-tang (short rib soup) or budae jjigae (army stew) at a cozy local eatery (₩13,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are available in English — check the official palace website and book 1–2 days ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the city wall trail.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Bukhansan National Park — Seoul's mountain escape. Take the subway to Gupabal Station and hike the Baegundae Peak trail or the more accessible Bukhansanseong Fortress trail. Spectacular winter views of the city below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Korea in Yongsan — one of Asia's largest museums with free admission. Explore Korean history from prehistoric times through the Joseon Dynasty with impressive artifacts and interactive exhibits.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner and evening in Itaewon — Seoul's most international neighborhood. Explore the diverse food scene and visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art area. Walk up Gyeongnidan-gil for trendy bars and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (GS25 or CU) — triangle kimbap, hot coffee, and egg sandwich (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Mountain trail packed lunch or snack from a trail vendor — dosirak (lunchbox) or cup ramyeon (₩5,000–8,000)
meals.dinner: Itaewon — Korean BBQ at a mid-range restaurant, samgyeopsal (pork belly) with all the banchan sides (₩18,000–25,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike early (by 9:00 AM) to allow time for the museum. Bukhansan trails can be icy in December — bring hiking poles or microspikes. The National Museum is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Namdaemun Market — Seoul's oldest and largest traditional market. Shop for Korean snacks, clothing, kitchenware, and souvenirs. Don't miss the fish cake (eomuk) and hotteok (sweet pancake) vendors warming up the cold morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) via cable car or a scenic hike up Namsan Mountain. Enjoy 360-degree views of Seoul from the observation deck. See the famous love lock fence and explore the surrounding Namsan Park.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Myeongdong — Seoul's premier shopping and K-beauty district. Browse flagship cosmetic stores (Innisfree, Etude House, Olive Young), sample endless street food, and soak in the festive December atmosphere with holiday decorations.

meals.breakfast: Namdaemun Market — hotteok (sweet cinnamon pancake) and eomuk (fish cake skewer) from market stalls (₩3,000–5,000)
meals.lunch: Namdaemun Market galbi-tang alley — hearty short rib soup with rice (₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Myeongdong street food crawl — tteokbokki, corn dog, grilled skewers, and bingsu (or hotteok for dessert) (₩15,000–20,000 total)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday markets are busiest — go to Namdaemun early (before 10:00 AM) to avoid peak crowds. Myeongdong is extremely lively on weekends. N Seoul Tower tickets cost around ₩21,000 for the observatory.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Jogyesa Temple — the head temple of Korean Buddhism, located right in Jongno-gu. Admire the ornate main hall, colorful lanterns, and the ancient white pine and zelkova trees. Attend a morning ceremony if timing allows. Explore the surrounding Buddhist culture street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Unhyeongung Palace — a lesser-visited royal residence with a more intimate atmosphere than the major palaces. Then explore the Seochon Village (west of Gyeongbokgung) — a neighborhood beloved by artists and writers with independent bookshops and cafes.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performance — check the Korea House or Jeongdong Theater for Nanta shows, traditional music (gugak), or mask dance (talchum) performances. Book tickets in advance for weekend shows.

meals.breakfast: Seochon Village café — nurungji (scorched rice porridge) or traditional Korean breakfast set (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Jongno-gu area — bibimbap at a traditional restaurant, served in a stone pot (dolsot bibimbap) (₩10,000–14,000)
meals.dinner: Korea House or nearby Insadong restaurant — hanjeongsik (Korean table d'hôte) with multiple small dishes (₩25,000–35,000)

day_by_day.notes: Jogyesa Temple is especially beautiful during the Lotus Lantern Festival, but December brings its own serene winter charm. Check Jeongdong Theater's schedule online — weekend performances often sell out.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (Namiseom) — a picturesque island famous for its tree-lined paths and the K-drama 'Winter Sonata.' Take the ITX train from Yongsan Station to Gapyeong, then a short ferry ride. The island is magical in winter with frost-covered trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Petite France or the Garden of Morning Calm (Achim Goyoh Arboretum) nearby — both are short bus rides from Gapyeong. The Garden of Morning Calm hosts a stunning winter lights festival in December.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by 7:00–8:00 PM. Relax with a quiet dinner near the hotel in Jongno-gu. Visit a traditional Korean jjimjilbang (sauna/bathhouse) for a restorative evening after a full day trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — grab and go before the early train (₩5,000–7,000)
meals.lunch: Nami Island restaurant — dak-galbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) or naengmyeon (cold noodles, a regional specialty) (₩13,000–18,000)
meals.dinner: Jongno-gu neighborhood pojangmacha or local restaurant — kimchi jjigae with rice and banchan (₩10,000–14,000)

day_by_day.notes: Leave by 8:00–9:00 AM to maximize time on the island. Nami Island entry is ₩16,000 (includes ferry). Garden of Morning Calm winter festival entry is around ₩11,000. Dress in multiple warm layers — it's colder outside the city.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) — a futuristic architectural landmark designed by Zaha Hadid. Visit the design museums inside, check out any current exhibitions, and walk the surrounding Dongdaemun History & Culture Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — a sobering and comprehensive museum covering Korean military history. Free admission. The outdoor exhibits of tanks, aircraft, and warships are impressive even in winter. Pair with a visit to the adjacent Yongsan Family Park.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Dongdaemun's famous night shopping scene — the massive fashion wholesale markets (Doota, Migliore, Hello APM) come alive after dark and stay open until 5:00 AM. Perfect for browsing K-fashion at affordable prices.

meals.breakfast: Jongno-gu café — Korean-style breakfast with congee (juk) and side dishes (₩8,000–12,000)
meals.lunch: Dongdaemun area — ox bone soup (seolleongtang) at a local restaurant, a Seoul specialty (₩12,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Dongdaemun night market stalls — dak-kkochi (chicken skewers), tteokbokki, and pajeon (scallion pancake) while shopping (₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: DDP often hosts special winter design exhibitions in December — check their website. The War Memorial is closed on Mondays, but Tuesday is perfect. Dongdaemun shopping is best after 10:00 PM for the full experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take the subway to Hongdae (Hongik University area) — Seoul's youth culture and indie music hub. Explore the street art murals, browse independent record stores, vintage clothing shops, and quirky K-pop merchandise stores. Visit the free walking street performers area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short ride to Sinchon and then Yeouido — visit the National Assembly building area and take a riverside walk along Hangang Park. In December, the park has winter festivals and food trucks. Rent a bicycle or simply stroll the riverside.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hongdae for the evening indie live music scene. Many small live music clubs (club FF, Rollinghall) host performances. Alternatively, explore the Sangsu-dong café street for a more relaxed evening with Korean craft beer and snacks.

meals.breakfast: Hongdae café — specialty coffee and Korean egg sandwich or avocado toast at a trendy local café (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Hongdae area — jokbal (braised pig's trotters) or bossam (boiled pork wraps) at a local specialty restaurant (₩15,000–20,000)
meals.dinner: Sangsu-dong or Hongdae — Korean fried chicken (chimaek) with Korean craft beer at a lively chicken-and-beer restaurant (₩20,000–28,000)

day_by_day.notes: Hongdae is at its most vibrant on weekday evenings — great for experiencing Seoul's youth culture. Check Rollinghall or Yes24 Live Hall for indie concert schedules in December.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Hannam-dong — one of Korea's finest private art museums featuring both traditional Korean art and contemporary international works. The building itself, designed by three world-renowned architects, is a masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hannam-dong and Itaewon's upscale Gyeongnidan-gil — browse concept stores, Korean designer boutiques, and international restaurants. Visit the Seoul Central Mosque (Korea's largest mosque) nearby for a cultural contrast.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve in Seoul! Myeongdong Cathedral is beautifully decorated and holds a special Christmas Eve mass — even non-religious visitors enjoy the atmosphere. Afterward, join the festive crowds in Myeongdong for Christmas markets, street performances, and holiday lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Jongno-gu bakery — patbingsu-inspired pastry or traditional rice cake (tteok) from a local tteok shop (₩6,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Hannam-dong — modern Korean fusion at a mid-range restaurant, try Korean-style pasta or grain bowl (₩15,000–22,000)
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve special — splurge slightly at a Korean BBQ restaurant in Itaewon or Myeongdong, premium galbi (beef short ribs) (₩30,000–40,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is one of Seoul's most festive nights — the city transforms with lights and celebrations. Book dinner in advance as popular restaurants fill up. Myeongdong Cathedral mass is at midnight; arrive early for a seat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Deoksugung Palace — the only palace open on Mondays and a wonderful Christmas morning walk. The stone-paved path along the palace wall (Deoksugung Doldam-gil) is one of Seoul's most romantic walks. Watch the Royal Guard Changing Ceremony at 11:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Seoul Museum of Art (SeMA) — free admission and excellent rotating exhibitions of Korean and international contemporary art. Then walk through Jung-gu's historic district to see the Bank of Korea Museum and old colonial-era architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Lotte World Tower's Sky Observatory (123rd floor) for spectacular Christmas night views of Seoul — the city glows beautifully in winter. Afterward, explore the Lotte World Mall and nearby Seokchon Lake, which has festive winter decorations.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or Jongno-gu — traditional Korean breakfast (kongnamul gukbap: bean sprout rice soup) at a local restaurant (₩8,000–10,000)
meals.lunch: Jung-gu area near Deoksugung — doenjang jjigae and japchae (glass noodles) set at a traditional Korean restaurant (₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Jamsil area near Lotte Tower — samgyeopsal (pork belly BBQ) or Korean hot pot (jeongol) at a lively restaurant (₩20,000–28,000)

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — most palaces and major attractions remain open. Lotte World Tower observatory tickets cost around ₩27,000; book online to skip queues. Seokchon Lake winter festival is free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) in Samcheong-dong — an excellent museum showcasing Korean contemporary art in a beautiful building with a lovely courtyard. Take time to explore the permanent collection and any special exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Gangnam-gu — explore the upscale Apgujeong Rodeo Street and Garosu-gil (Tree-lined Street) in Sinsa-dong. Browse Korean designer fashion, K-beauty concept stores, and the neighborhood that inspired PSY's 'Gangnam Style.' Visit the COEX Mall and its famous Starfield Library.
day_by_day.evening: Final proper evening in Seoul — return to a favorite neighborhood for a farewell dinner. Consider a traditional Korean cooking class in the early evening (book in advance through platforms like Airbnb Experiences or Class101) followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Samcheong-dong café — specialty latte and Korean-style French toast or injeolmi (rice cake) waffle (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.lunch: Gangnam area — Korean cold noodles (naengmyeon) or spicy beef soup (yukgaejang) at a local restaurant (₩12,000–16,000)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — jjimdak (braised chicken) or haemul pajeon (seafood pancake) with makgeolli (Korean rice wine) at a traditional restaurant (₩20,000–30,000)

day_by_day.notes: MMCA Samcheong is closed on Mondays — Saturday is ideal. Garosu-gil is particularly pleasant for an afternoon stroll. Book a cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance; they fill up quickly on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — revisit a favorite spot or explore anything missed. Jongno-gu's Tapgol Park (Korea's first modern public park) is a peaceful morning stop. Browse Insadong one last time for last-minute souvenirs: traditional tea, hanji paper crafts, Korean snacks, and ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — pack up, check out, and head to Incheon Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before international flight departure. The AREX express train from Seoul Station takes 43 minutes to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Incheon Airport. Enjoy a final Korean meal in the airport's food court — Korean Air's terminal has excellent bibimbap and doenjang jjigae options at reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast — haejang-guk (hangover soup / hearty beef bone soup) at a local Jongno-gu restaurant, a classic Seoul morning meal (₩10,000–14,000)
meals.lunch: Insadong — light lunch of mandu (dumplings) and japchae at a casual restaurant before heading to the airport (₩10,000–15,000)
meals.dinner: Incheon Airport — Korean restaurant in the terminal, bibimbap or samgak kimbap for a final taste of Korea (₩12,000–18,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check airline baggage limits — Korean snacks, cosmetics, and souvenirs add up quickly! Duty-free shopping at Incheon Airport is world-class. Return T-money card at the airport for a refund on remaining balance. Keep ₩50,000–100,000 in cash for last-day expenses.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Seoul, South Korea Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00 at Incheon International Airport
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer via luxury chauffeur service to Jongno-gu Boutique Stay. Check-in, unpack, and freshen up. Take a gentle orientation stroll through the historic Bukchon Hanok Village lanes just steps from the hotel — admire the traditional tiled rooftops and narrow alleys at your own pace
day_by_day.evening: Explore Insadong's lantern-lit streets and artisan galleries for a soft introduction to Seoul's cultural soul. Browse premium Korean craft shops for initial souvenir scouting

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at Incheon Airport — visit Seven Luck or the premium food hall at Terminal 1 for a light Korean set meal upon landing
meals.lunch: No formal lunch — light snack at the hotel upon arrival (request welcome refreshments from the boutique stay)
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul (2 Michelin stars) in Gangnam — modern Korean fine dining with a tasting menu showcasing elevated hansik. Reservation strongly recommended in advance

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in confirmation with the hotel before arrival. Keep Day 1 light to recover from long-haul travel. December in Seoul is cold (0–5°C), so pack thermal layers, a heavy coat, and gloves.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Gyeongbokgung Palace at opening time (9:00 AM) — witness the Changing of the Royal Guard ceremony at 10:00 AM. Rent a premium hanbok from a nearby boutique rental house (Hanboknam or Knot) for an immersive royal experience and complimentary palace entry
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Korea (Yongsan) via private car — explore Korea's most comprehensive collection of artifacts spanning 5,000 years. Spend 2–3 hours in the permanent galleries including the gold crowns of Silla and Goryeo celadon ceramics
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Cheonggyecheon Stream promenade, beautifully illuminated in winter. End at Gwanghwamun Square for night views of the palace and Yi Sun-sin statue

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or nearby Café Bora in Insadong for their signature purple taro latte and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Tosokchon Samgyetang — legendary ginseng chicken soup restaurant near Gyeongbokgung, a Seoul institution serving premium slow-cooked whole chicken in medicinal broth
meals.dinner: Mingles (1 Michelin star), Gangnam — chef Mingoo Kang's celebrated Korean-European fusion tasting menu with exceptional wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Gyeongbokgung opens at 9:00 AM (closed Tuesdays — confirm schedule). Book hanbok rental the evening before. Wear warm layers under the hanbok for outdoor photos in December cold.

day_by_day.morning: Private cultural workshop at a traditional Korean tea ceremony studio in Insadong — learn the art of darye (tea ritual) with a master practitioner in an intimate setting. Follow with a visit to Jogyesa Temple, the head temple of Korean Buddhism, beautifully decorated with winter lanterns
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Whanki Museum or the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art (MMCA) Seoul branch in Sogyeok-dong — world-class Korean modern art in an architecturally stunning setting. Spend 2 hours browsing curated contemporary Korean works
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bukchon Hanok Village by twilight — the golden lantern glow against traditional hanok rooftops is magical in December. Visit a premium makgeolli (rice wine) tasting bar in the neighborhood

meals.breakfast: Gwanghwamun Guksi — a beloved local breakfast spot serving handmade noodle soups; try the guksu with anchovy broth
meals.lunch: Sanchon Restaurant in Insadong — a serene temple food (사찰음식) dining experience in a hanok setting; vegetarian Buddhist cuisine with seasonal mountain vegetables
meals.dinner: Gaon (3 Michelin stars) — the pinnacle of Korean fine dining in Gangnam; prix-fixe menu celebrating royal court cuisine with impeccable tableware and service

day_by_day.notes: Book Gaon at least 2–3 weeks in advance — one of the hardest reservations in Seoul. The tea ceremony workshop should be reserved through your hotel concierge. MMCA is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day tour of Changdeokgung Palace and the Secret Garden (Huwon) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The Secret Garden winter landscape with bare trees and frozen ponds is hauntingly beautiful. Hire a licensed English-speaking palace guide
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Changgyeonggung Palace next door, then walk through the historic Naksan Park trail along Seoul's ancient fortress walls for panoramic city views. Stop at the Ihwa Mural Village for street art exploration
day_by_day.evening: Head to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) for its futuristic architecture illuminated at night — explore the design museum and any ongoing exhibitions. Browse the late-night Dongdaemun fashion market for premium Korean designer pieces

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Anthracite Coffee Roasters (Huam-dong location) for specialty single-origin coffee and artisan pastries in a converted industrial space
meals.lunch: Hadongkwan — Seoul's most historic gomtang (beef bone broth) restaurant, operating since 1939 near Myeongdong; simple, deeply nourishing, and culturally significant
meals.dinner: Balwoo Gongyang at the Templestay Information Center — award-winning temple cuisine with a modern presentation; a refined, meditative dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Secret Garden tours are guided and run at fixed times — book in advance. Dress warmly for the outdoor garden walk. DDP exhibitions change seasonally — check the current program before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day K-culture immersion: Begin with a private K-pop industry tour — visit HYBE Insight (the BTS museum and interactive experience center) in Yongsan for an in-depth look at the global K-pop phenomenon
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue K-culture exploration at SM Town COEX Artium in Gangnam — interactive K-pop museum, hologram theater, and official merchandise. Walk through Gangnam's Apgujeong Rodeo Street — Seoul's luxury fashion district with Korean designer boutiques, concept stores, and celebrity-frequented cafés
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live K-pop showcase or idol fan signing event (check Melon Ticket or Interpark for December schedules). Alternatively, visit a premium norebang (karaoke) suite — book a luxury private room at Su Norebang in Gangnam

meals.breakfast: Egg Drop — Seoul's iconic gourmet egg sandwich chain; visit the Apgujeong flagship for premium avocado and truffle egg sandwiches
meals.lunch: Hanilkwan — a Seoul institution since 1939 serving classic Korean table d'hôte (hanjeongsik) meals in Gangnam; traditional multi-course dining with banchan
meals.dinner: Mosu Seoul (1 Michelin star) — chef Sung Anh's innovative seasonal Korean tasting menu with international techniques; intimate, avant-garde, and exceptional

day_by_day.notes: HYBE Insight requires advance ticket booking online — sell out quickly on weekends. Check HYBE's official website for December operating hours. Norebang rooms should be reserved same-day by phone or app.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nami Island (Namiseom) via private car and ferry — a romantic island famous for its tree-lined avenues, now dusted in winter frost. Walk the iconic metasequoia and birch tree paths in peaceful winter quiet
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Petite France and the Garden of Morning Calm (Achim-go-yo Jeongwon) on the return — the garden hosts a spectacular winter illumination festival in December, one of Korea's most beautiful light events
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul by private car. Decompress with a premium jjimjilbang (Korean spa) experience at Dragon Hill Spa in Yongsan — enjoy gender-separated hot baths, saunas, and relaxation rooms

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — request a packed premium breakfast box from the boutique stay if departing before 8:00 AM
meals.lunch: On Nami Island — dine at the island's Naminara Republic restaurant for hearty Korean comfort food including dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) and bibimbap
meals.dinner: Congdu — elegant Korean cuisine in a renovated hanok in Jongno-gu; close to the hotel; seasonal menu with premium Korean ingredients in a refined traditional setting

day_by_day.notes: Nami Island is approximately 1.5 hours from Seoul — depart by 8:30 AM for a comfortable day. The Garden of Morning Calm Winter Illumination Festival typically runs November–January; confirm 2027 dates. Book Dragon Hill Spa towel/robe service in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class in a traditional hanok kitchen — learn to prepare 4–5 signature Korean dishes including kimchi jeon (kimchi pancake), japchae (glass noodles), and doenjang jjigae (soybean paste stew) with a professional Korean chef
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gwangjang Market — Seoul's oldest and most atmospheric covered market. Take a premium food tour with a local guide to sample bindaetteok (mung bean pancakes), mayak gimbap (sesame rice rolls), and raw beef yukhoe without the crowds
day_by_day.evening: Visit N Seoul Tower (Namsan Tower) via private cable car — enjoy 360° panoramic night views of the glittering Seoul skyline. Attach a love lock on the fence as a travel memory

meals.breakfast: Noryangjin Fish Market premium sashimi breakfast — visit the live seafood auction market and choose your own fresh fish for an on-site breakfast prepared to order (arrange via guide)
meals.lunch: Post-cooking class lunch — enjoy the dishes you prepared with your chef instructor, paired with traditional Korean teas and makgeolli
meals.dinner: Byeokje Galbi — Seoul's most prestigious galbi (grilled short rib) restaurant; premium USDA and Korean Hanwoo beef aged in-house; a carnivore's pinnacle experience

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class through O'ngo Food Communications or Coreana Cultural Foundation — both offer premium English-language classes in traditional settings. Gwangjang Market is most vibrant in the afternoon. N Seoul Tower is spectacular on clear winter nights — check visibility forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art in Hannam-dong — one of Asia's finest private art museums housing Korean national treasures alongside international contemporary works by Damien Hirst, Anish Kapoor, and Korean masters
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Itaewon and Hannam-dong — Seoul's most cosmopolitan neighborhood. Browse concept stores (Boon The Shop, 10 Corso Como Seoul), independent galleries, and the boutique-lined streets of Hannam-dong's creative district
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Korean performing arts show — book tickets for a performance at the National Theater of Korea (Namsan) featuring jeongganbo music, pansori (Korean opera), or a contemporary fusion performance

meals.breakfast: Tartine Manufactory Seoul in Hannam-dong — the acclaimed San Francisco bakery's Seoul outpost; exceptional sourdough, pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Ottogi in Itaewon — premium Korean-French fusion bistro; elegant seasonal menu with Korean ingredients interpreted through French technique
meals.dinner: La Yeon (3 Michelin stars) at The Shilla Hotel — the most celebrated Korean fine dining restaurant in Seoul; royal court cuisine with flawless presentation and impeccable service overlooking the city

day_by_day.notes: Leeum Museum may have temporary closures — confirm opening hours in advance. La Yeon requires reservations weeks in advance and has a smart dress code. The National Theater of Korea program should be checked and booked online before the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan — an emotionally powerful and architecturally impressive museum chronicling Korean history from ancient battles to the Korean War; allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Seochon Village (West Village) — the charming, lesser-known sister neighborhood to Bukchon; browse independent bookshops, artist studios, and heritage cafés. Visit Gyeonghuigung Palace, a quieter royal palace perfect for contemplative exploration
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Eve celebration — Seoul goes all-out for Christmas. Stroll through the festively illuminated Myeongdong district, visit명동성당 (Myeongdong Cathedral) beautifully lit for the season, and browse the outdoor Christmas market stalls

meals.breakfast: Café Onion Anguk — a stunning renovated hanok café in Bukchon; famous for their jumbo croissant and specialty coffee in a visually breathtaking courtyard setting
meals.lunch: Gwanghwamun Jip — beloved traditional Korean restaurant near the palace district serving premium doenjang jjigae and grilled mackerel set meals
meals.dinner: Jungsik Seoul revisit or Dalgona — elegant modern Korean in Seochon; seasonal tasting menu in an intimate hanok dining room with natural wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The War Memorial of Korea is free to enter and closed on Mondays. Seochon is best explored on foot — wear comfortable warm shoes. Myeongdong gets extremely crowded in the Christmas season — visit after 8 PM for a more atmospheric experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hike up Inwangsan Mountain (338m) — accessible directly from Jongno-gu; the fortress wall trail offers stunning winter views over the city at dawn. Visit the shamanist Guksadang shrine along the way for a uniquely Korean spiritual experience
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium Korean beauty and wellness experience — visit Sulwhasoo Flagship Store in Insadong for a complimentary skincare consultation and traditional Korean herbal beauty treatment. Explore Amorepacific Museum of Art (APMA) in Yongsan for curated contemporary art
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve luxury dinner and celebration — attend a Christmas Eve gala dinner or special menu at one of Seoul's iconic rooftop restaurants

meals.breakfast: Post-hike warming breakfast at a local pojangmacha (street food tent) near Inwangsan — hearty tteokbokki (spicy rice cakes), odeng (fish cake soup), and hotteok (sweet pancakes)
meals.lunch: Kwon Sookhee's Hanshik Jinjin — premium traditional Korean lunch set in a beautiful Jongno hanok; seasonal banchan and premium doenjang soup
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at Four Seasons Hotel Seoul's Boccalino or Yu Yuan — book the special Christmas Eve multi-course menu with wine pairing and live music; a memorable luxury celebration

day_by_day.notes: Inwangsan hike takes approximately 1.5–2 hours round trip; depart by 6:30 AM for sunrise. Dress in full thermal layers. The Four Seasons Christmas Eve dinner sells out months in advance — book immediately upon confirming travel. Sulwhasoo Flagship offers English-speaking beauty consultants.

day_by_day.morning: Peaceful Christmas morning — visit Jogyesa Temple for the serene morning bell ceremony. Walk through the quiet, lantern-decorated temple grounds. Alternatively, attend Christmas Mass at the historic Myeongdong Cathedral — a moving experience regardless of faith
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Suwon Hwaseong Fortress — a UNESCO World Heritage Site, 45 minutes from Seoul by private car. Walk the 5.7km fortress walls surrounding the historic city, visit the palace complex, and explore the traditional folk village nearby
day_by_day.evening: Return to Seoul for a relaxed Christmas evening. Visit a premium jjimjilbang for a long soak, or enjoy in-room premium room service and a Korean drama marathon — the ultimate cozy Korean winter evening

meals.breakfast: Hotel Christmas breakfast — request a special holiday breakfast spread from the boutique stay; supplement with pastries from a nearby artisan bakery
meals.lunch: Suwon's famous Wangkalbi — the city is legendary for its galbi (grilled short ribs); dine at Yeongdong Galbi near Hwaseong for the authentic Suwon-style bone-in galbi experience
meals.dinner: Ryunique — innovative Korean tasting menu in Gangnam; chef Ryu Tae-hwan's playful, technically brilliant cuisine with seasonal Korean ingredients in a relaxed fine dining atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day is a public holiday in South Korea — many attractions and restaurants operate on reduced hours. Confirm Suwon Hwaseong opening times in advance. Book Ryunique well ahead. The fortress walk takes 2–3 hours and is exposed to wind — dress very warmly.

day_by_day.morning: Premium Korean pottery and celadon workshop — take a private masterclass at a Jongno-gu ceramics studio; create your own piece inspired by the Goryeo celadon tradition under expert guidance. The studio will glaze and ship your finished piece home
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ihwa Mural Village and Naksan Park for street art and fortress wall views. Descend to Hyehwa (Daehangno) — Seoul's university arts district; browse independent theaters, art book stores, and quirky concept cafés
day_by_day.evening: Final major cultural evening — attend a performance of the National Gugak Center's traditional Korean music and dance performance, or book tickets for a contemporary Korean theater production in Daehangno

meals.breakfast: Café Mamas in Hyehwa — beloved neighborhood breakfast spot; Korean-style morning set with rice, soup, and seasonal banchan
meals.lunch: Seoulsik — modern Korean restaurant in Insadong serving elevated versions of Korean street food classics with premium ingredients and beautiful plating
meals.dinner: Soigné (1 Michelin star) — chef Jun Lee's intimate 12-seat restaurant offering a single seasonal tasting menu that changes daily; one of Seoul's most creative and personal dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: The pottery workshop should be booked through the hotel concierge at least 3–4 days in advance. Soigné has very limited seating — book as early as possible. Daehangno is best explored on foot in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Seoul — wake up early for a last walk through Bukchon Hanok Village and Gyeongbokgung area as the city stirs to life. Visit Insadong one last time for any final premium souvenir shopping — Korean lacquerware, hanji paper crafts, celadon pottery, or premium red ginseng sets
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Jongno-gu Boutique Stay. Private luxury chauffeur transfer to Incheon International Airport. Arrive at least 3 hours before international departure. Browse the premium duty-free shops at Incheon — one of the world's best airport retail experiences
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the warmth of Seoul's culture, cuisine, and beauty home

meals.breakfast: Final Korean breakfast at Tosokchon or a nearby sundubu jjigae (soft tofu stew) restaurant — a warming, soul-satisfying farewell meal in the cold winter morning
meals.lunch: Incheon Airport — dine at the premium Korean restaurant on the departure level for a final taste of bibimbap or galbi tang (short rib soup) before boarding
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout from the boutique stay if your flight departs in the evening — most luxury properties accommodate this. Pack Korean skincare products, food items (check customs regulations for your destination), and any purchased artworks carefully. Keep all receipts for VAT refund at the airport — tourists can claim back 10% VAT on purchases over ₩30,000 at the Global Blue or Korea Tax Free counters at Incheon.

query: Seoul K-culture and food, $2200 couple, winter 2026 from LAX
